checks.detail: field.power == 1.0000118 against the 1.0000002 the docs page prints -- a 1.2e-5 difference. Both are the float32 normalisation residue of a 512x512 plane wave, so the physics is identical and only the last digits differ: the published page was built from a different commit than the pinned d24bdf0. Recorded rather than papered over, because a reader comparing digit-for-digit would otherwise think something was wrong.
checks.name: plane_wave_power_is_unity_but_not_upstreams_exact_digits

demonstrates: chromatix.functional.plane_wave / square_pupil / transfer_propagate, the Spectrum density weighting and ChromaticScalarField, and the chromatix.elements / chromatix.systems composition layer (OpticalSystem, PlaneWave, FFLens, ClearThinSample, BasicSensor, Microscope, Optical4FSystemPSF, utils.siemens_star).
notes: Field.intensity sums the density-weighted per-wavelength intensities, so a two-wavelength field with densities summing to 1 has the same mean intensity as the equivalent monochromatic field, while Field.power stays 1 PER wavelength. A consumer that multiplies power by density double-counts.
